claims.claim: First open-source, native 1-bit LLM at the 2-billion parameter scale, trained on 4T tokens
claims.quote: We introduce BitNet b1.58 2B4T, the first open-source, native 1-bit Large Lan- guage Model (LLM) at the 2-billion parameter scale.

claims.claim: Native 1-bit LLM trained at scale achieves performance comparable to leading full-precision open-weight models of similar size
claims.quote: The core contribution of this work is to demonstrate that a native 1-bit LLM, when trained effectively at scale, can achieve performance comparable

claims.claim: Significant efficiency advantages: reduced memory footprint, energy consumption and decoding latency
claims.quote: while offering significant advantages in computational efficiency, including sub- stantially reduced memory footprint, energy consumption, and decoding latency.

claims.claim: Release of weights plus open-source inference implementations for GPU and CPU (custom CUDA kernel, bitnet.cpp)
claims.quote: the model weights are released via Hugging Face along with open-source inference implementations for both GPU and CPU architectures.

claims.claim: Architectural innovations specific to the 1-bit paradigm (BitLinear layers with ternary absmean weights, 8-bit activations, subln, ReLU2)
claims.quote: trained from scratch on a substantial dataset of 4 trillion tokens, leveraging architectural and training innovations specific to the 1-bit paradigm.
claims.ablation_quote: BitNet b1.58 2B4T maintains stronger overall performance than the INT4 quantized versions of Qwen2.5-1.5B on the evaluated benchmarks.

claims.claim: Training innovations specific to 1-bit training (two-stage high-LR/cooldown schedule, two-stage weight decay, summed SFT loss)
claims.quote: trained from scratch on a substantial dataset of 4 trillion tokens, leveraging architectural and training innovations specific to the 1-bit paradigm.

rerun.quote: All models are instruction-tuned versions. We re-run all benchmarks with a public evaluation pipeline for a fair comparison.

scores_copied.quote: We re-run all benchmarks with a public evaluation pipeline for a fair comparison.

data_disclosure.quote: The pre-training corpus comprised a mixture of publicly available text and code datasets, including large web crawls like DCLM (Li et al., 2024b) and educational web pages like FineWeb-EDU

tokens_disclosed.quote: Trained on a corpus of 4 trillion tokens, the model has been rigorously evaluated across benchmarks

coding.note: ARCH ablation coded PARTIAL: the only evidence is comparisons against full-precision and PTQ models, which differ in size, data and token count. There is no matched with/without study of BitLinear, subln or ReLU2. The training-schedule innovations (two-stage LR and WD, summed loss) have no comparison, so they are coded NO; the summed-loss benefit is asserted only as 'empirically observed'. BitLinear comes from the authors' prior BitNet work and is cited as such, so it is not counted as a rename. Data is PARTIAL: sources are named but no proportions are given.
